title: The Repetition Advantage in Long-CoT SFT is a Termination Effect

contributions.purpose: Determine whether the 'repetition advantage' in long-CoT SFT reflects improved reasoning or merely better output termination behavior.
contributions.mechanism: A diagnostic framework that decomposes accuracy into ParseRate (fraction of parseable outputs) and Acc|Parse (accuracy conditional on successful parsing).
contributions.evaluation: Applied to repetition vs data-scaling SFT conditions on AIME and GPQA benchmarks, revealing the repetition advantage is primarily a termination effect.
contributions.source_quote: A diagnostic framework decomposing long-CoT accuracy into ParseRate and Acc|Parse, revealing that the repetition advantage in SFT is primarily a termination effect rather than improved reasoning.

contributions.purpose: Quantify how much of the repetition-vs-scaling accuracy gap is explained by parseability rather than reasoning quality.
contributions.mechanism: Mediation analysis conditioning the accuracy gap on successful parsing across repetition and data-scaling conditions.
contributions.evaluation: Mediation fractions exceed 1.0 and the accuracy gap reverses on AIME benchmarks when conditioning on successful parsing, indicating data scaling actually produces better reasoning when both models terminate properly.
contributions.source_quote: A mediation analysis showing that parseability over-explains the accuracy gap between repetition and scaling conditions, with the gap reversing on AIME benchmarks when conditioning on successful parsing.

contributions.purpose: Partially address termination behavior without requiring data repetition.
contributions.mechanism: Termination-Aware SFT, which increases the loss weight on termination tokens (</think> and EOS) during fine-tuning.
contributions.evaluation: Improves accuracy by 2.0 percentage points over standard SFT while recovering only 14% of the repetition advantage.
contributions.source_quote: Termination-Aware SFT, a targeted intervention that improves accuracy by 2.0pp through explicit termination token reweighting, demonstrating that termination behavior can be partially addressed without data repetition.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work complements these studies by examining a specific failure mode in long-CoT SFT: the difficulty of learning proper termination behavior.
Kopiczko et al. (2026) made the surprising observation that repeating a small dataset outperforms training on a larger diverse dataset—the phenomenon our work investigates.
Our work extends this line of research by identifying termination behavior as a critical factor in long-CoT SFT and proposing Termination-Aware SFT as a targeted intervention.

notes: Proposed intervention (Termination-Aware SFT) recovers only 14% of the repetition advantage; the paper itself frames this as evidence that termination learning involves mechanisms beyond explicit loss reweighting (partially negative result).
